data.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py::test_code_review_sidecar_emit_two_clone_union`
fails intermittently in CI when the two-clone fixture's `git push origin HEAD:tickets`
returns exit 1. It cost Gerrit change 1655 a spurious `Verified -1` (ticket
satisfied-emerald-grayling), the second time this fixture family has taxed an unrelated
change — chewed-illicit-blacklemur (b8f7-65be-ec00-4844) records the first, against change
1640.

This is a SIBLING of willing-cellular-carp (1647-19b3-cbec-4a17), not a regression of it.
Carp's fix was correct for the race it targeted (the two-clone **base precondition** sync).
Its commit 78257ce2ff is ALREADY an ancestor of the failing patchset, so the remedy is
proven incomplete for THIS manifestation rather than wrong: the failure here is in the
**push** leg, not the base-precondition setup.

## Evidence

- CI run 31628153181, leg `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.11)`, xdist worker gw0.
  `subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['git','push','-q','origin','HEAD:tickets']'
  returned non-zero exit status 1`, raised from `_assert_emit_is_append_only`
  (test_concurrency_regression.py:1714).
- 78257ce2ff ("De-flake two-clone sidecar base precondition") is an ancestor of the failing
  commit — verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`.
- LANE SHAPE: 1 of 5 lanes failed. The unit lane passed entirely (12320 passed, 66 skipped).
  A deterministic defect in the change under test failed EVERY lane on its earlier
  patchsets, so one-of-five plus a sidecar-fixture test is the flake signature, not a
  code signature.
- NOT LOCALLY REPRODUCIBLE: passes standalone, and the whole file passes 3/3 under CI's
  exact parallel settings (`-n 4 --dist loadgroup`).
- The change under test (1655) is the Jira reconciler's outbound link path and imports
  nothing the failing test exercises — zero linkage, verified by grep rather than assumed.

## Lead worth checking FIRST

The base the failing run used, cc69cc1179 "Retry the write lock instead of losing writes",
changes tickets-store write-lock RETRY — the very subsystem this fixture stresses by racing
two clones at the same remote. An interaction between the new retry behaviour and the
fixture's push leg is plausible and cheap to check before hunting elsewhere.

Also cross-check depraved-frowzy-trout: its 23-site audit landed in this same file, so the
push-race sites may sit in either its converted or its deliberately-kept set. If a push site
was KEPT as fail-fast on purpose, that decision and this flake need reconciling.

## Scope

Identify the race in the push leg of the two-clone sidecar fixture family
(`test_code_review_*`, `test_plan_review_*`, `test_completion_*`
`_sidecar_emit_two_clone_union`) and make the fixture deterministic. Do NOT paper over it
with a blanket retry that would also mask a genuine push regression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The failing push leg's race is identified and named in a comment on this ticket, with
      the mechanism stated (which two operations interleave, and on which clone).
- [ ] The fixture is deterministic under CI's settings — verified by running the affected
      file under `-n 4 --dist loadgroup` in a loop (>=20 iterations) with zero failures.
- [ ] The fix distinguishes fixture-setup racing from a real push failure — verified by a
      test or assertion that still fails when the push genuinely cannot succeed.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py`
      pass.
data.title: Two-clone sidecar fixture races on the tickets push leg
